answer: Trust propagates through a bounded number of steps of a normalized random walk on the attestation graph, whose transition kernel limits how far endorsements can spread. A sybil cluster with few links to honest nodes has low conductance: the sparse external cut constrains incoming trusted mass, so, under capped node weights, min-cut and transitivity bounds limit its aggregate voting weight. Its influence cannot grow merely by adding accounts, though a broad honest boundary can raise it. The resulting trust terrace resists echo-driven inflation.
